worldcombat.skill.leechseed.summary: Throw a seed along your aim: on impact a root burrows into a foe and sips a share of its maximum health every few seconds, feeding the caster. The seed withers when it expires, is cured, the target falls, or the caster leaves; grass types and already-seeded targets cannot take it, walls stop the seed, and an empty throw just falls.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.use.0: Turn a hard fight into a war of attrition and grow your health back
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.use.1: Keep a lasting siphon running on a foe
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.use.2: Open the gap and let the root bleed the foe for you
Reach %1$s blocks; the seed flies along your aim and walls stop it. Once rooted the seed lasts %2$s. Grass types cannot be seeded, nor can a target that already carries a seed.

The root sips every %1$s, taking %2$s of the target's maximum health (at least 1) and healing the caster by the actual amount. It withers when the target falls, the seed expires, it is cured, or the caster leaves.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.gluttony.on: Gluttony: each sip x1.35 and the interval x0.75 to work faster; the seed lasts x0.7.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.gluttony.off: Slow sip: the seed lasts x1.25 and the interval x1.15, drawing longer and steadier; the sip itself is unchanged.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.timing: Seed along your aim: after %2$s of preparation it spends %4$s PP; the recovery is %3$s, the cooldown %5$s, and the current range %1$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.growth.0: At level %1$s the reach grows to %2$s blocks and the seed lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.growth.1: At level %1$s the reach grows to %2$s blocks and the seed lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.preference.g: Gluttony: sip x1.35, interval x0.75, duration x0.7, similar total but felt sooner. Slow sip: duration x1.25, interval x1.15, drawing longer and steadier.
worldcombat.skill.leechseed.preference.a: The partner only seeds while a threat is this close; smaller keeps it for melee, larger chases out to plant the root.
Below this health ratio the partner seeds to sustain itself first; above it, seeding is an ordinary control action.
When on, the partner will also leave its post to seed.
